source_text: XI. Nam cum Montanus cum Iuliano habuisset sermones aliquos ob eam mulierem quae ad nostram communionem obrepsit, quae non communicabat, cumque post correptionem quam in eum congesserat in frigore ipso discordiae mansisset, ostensum est eadem nocte Montano hoc. Visum est, inquit, mihi venisse ad nos centuriones. cumque deducerent nos per viam longam, pervenimus in campum immensum, in quo nobis occurrerunt Cyprianus et Leucius. pervenimus autem in locum candidum, et facta sunt vestimenta nostra candida et caro nostra commutata candidior vestimentis nostris candidis. ita autem perlucida fuit caro nostra, ut oculorum visum ad intima cordis admitteret. respiciens in pectus meum video quasdam sordes, et experrectus sum in visione. et occurrit mihi Lucianus, et retuli illi visionem, et aio illi: Scis quia sordes illae illud est quod non statim concordavi cum Iuliano? et in hoc experrectus sum. qua de re, fratres dilectissimi, concordiam, pacem, unanimitatem omni virtute teneamus. imitemur iam hic esse quod ibi futuri sumus. si nos invitant iustis promissa praemia, si terret iniustis poena praedicta, si cum Christo esse et regnare cupimus, quae ad Christum et ad regnum ducant, illa faciamus. optamus vos bene valere.
pass_a_gloss: Literal thread: since Montanus had had some talks with Julian about the woman who crept into our communion though not communicating, and since after the rebuke he had heaped on him he had remained in the chill of disagreement, this was shown to Montanus that same night; centurions seemed to come and lead them by a long road to a vast plain where Cyprian and Leucius met them and to a shining place where clothes turned white and flesh turned whiter than the clothes and so translucent that sight reached the heart’s interior; looking at his breast he sees stains and wakes in the vision, tells Lucianus that the stains are his delay in agreeing with Julian, and fully wakes; therefore the writer urges dearest brothers to hold concord, peace, unanimity with all strength, to imitate here what they will be there, to do what leads to Christ and the kingdom if promised rewards and foretold punishment move them and if they desire to be and reign with Christ, and closes with a farewell wish.
pass_b_english: For when Montanus had held several conversations with Julianus concerning that woman who had crept into our communion without truly sharing in it, and when after the rebuke he had poured upon him he had still remained in the very chill of their disagreement, this was shown to Montanus that same night.

As he said, It seemed to me that centurions came to us, and while they led us along a long road we arrived at an immense plain, where Cyprian and Leucius met us, and then we came to a shining white place, and our garments became white and our flesh was changed to something whiter than our white garments, and our flesh was so translucent that the gaze of the eyes reached into the inward parts of the heart.

Looking upon my breast I see certain stains, and I awoke within the vision, and Lucianus met me, and I related the vision to him and said to him, Do you know that those stains are this, that I did not immediately make peace with Julianus.
And upon this I fully awoke.
On this account, dearest brothers, let us hold fast to concord, peace, and oneness of mind with all our strength.
Let us imitate already here what we shall be there.

If the promised rewards for the just invite us, if the foretold punishment for the unjust terrifies us, if we desire to be with Christ and to reign with him, let us do those things that lead to Christ and to the kingdom.

choices.english: in the very chill of the quarrel
choices.why: ablative of attendant circumstance; frigus is metaphorical coldness after heated rebuke, not weather
rejected: in the frost itself of winter

choices.why: facta sunt with predicate adjective marks changed state in the vision, not merely that they were white before
concordare cum takes comitative sense of coming into agreement after discord, context is reconciliation
